rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>Let me tell you about <color(4)>Gain Bijou<ce()><thumbnail(185)>, the man we are about to meet up with.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>The guy is an <book(55)>Exodus<endbook()> contractor who goes by the alias Black Southern Cross.
rows.notes: Black Southern Cross per character_names_021 nickname.

rows.en: <operator(30060,1)><speed(2)><book(55)>Exodus<endbook()> is the act of <book(54)>Domepolis<endbook()> residents escaping <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> control and moving to live on fertile land.
<operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>All over Siberia there are cities run by the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> that are called <book(54)>Domepolis<endbook()><thumbnail(186)>.
<operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>A <book(54)>Domepolis<endbook()> holds not only ordinary citizens; monks of a sect called <book(83)>Vodarac<endbook()> and political prisoners are confined there too.
<operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>They are run by what is called the <book(56)>Siberian Railway<endbook()><thumbnail(187)>, a subordinate body of the <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>.
<operator(30060,1)><speed(2)>The <book(56)>Siberian Railway<endbook()> defines <book(55)>Exodus<endbook()> as a serious crime; merely planning one brings severe punishment.
<topic()><operator(30110,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Gain<ce()> is hunted by the <book(56)>Siberian Railway<endbook()> as a top-class bounty head. That is why he teamed up with us.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>The goal of this operation is to work with <color(4)>Gain<ce()> and make the <book(55)>Exodus<endbook()><thumbnail(188)> succeed.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>And one more thing... Breaking out a <book(83)>Vodarac<endbook()> high priest who is due to be executed soon.
rows.notes: Source has no subject; gerund keeps it open.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>The place is a <book(54)>Domepolis<endbook()> called Wulgusk. The high priest was thrown into prison as a political prisoner on false charges.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Gain<ce()> has teamed up with residents inside and already managed to slip into the <book(54)>Domepolis<endbook()> prison.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>The moment the <book(55)>Exodus<endbook()> starts, we back up <color(4)>Gain<ce()> and get the high priest out. You get the gist, right?
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Gain<ce()> is well versed in all kinds of information. Meeting up with him should be a great advantage for our actions from here on.
rows.notes: Operator id is Holland (30110) although the register (wareware / kare) sounds like Jamil; see uncertainties.

rows.en: <thumbdown()><operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>It'd be a big help to have you people on board. I'm counting on you.

uncertainties.issue: "ukeoinin" rendered "contractor" (character_names_021 role says "Exodus specialist"); no locked term found.
Domepolis used unchanged as plural ("cities ... called Domepolis") to keep the book span on the locked spelling.

Operator tag says Holland (30110) but the wording is formal (wareware, kare) unlike his other lines (ore-tachi, yatsu) and like Jamil's. Translated in a neutral register; possible source-data speaker slip, not changed.
In this game's crossover setting the Vodarac (Eureka Seven) are held in King Gainer's Domepolis; "high priest" for kousou is descriptive, English E7 usage not verified.

glossary_proposals.why: King Gainer Domepolis where the Exodus starts; not in glossary.
Title of the Vodarac cleric to be rescued in missions 06; needs one project-wide term.

Slot 23 ruling: "high priest" for kousou matches the term already used and proposed in dialogue batch_01895/01975 (mission 06) and briefing 4003521; consistent.
Slot 28: gerund keeps the source's missing subject open; "due to be executed soon" correct.
Slot 29: "Wulgusk" is in no glossary file; it matches the common English King Gainer spelling; provisional.
Slots 19, 22, 24, 27: <thumbnail> follows the same noun as in the source.
Gain is male in character_names_021 and the source itself says otoko/kare.
